correctness.rationale: Choose a unit center on one unused coordinate and average \(m\) slices supported on distinct other coordinates. Slice membership forces each selected vector's off-coordinate tail to have norm at most \(\eta_\delta=(1-(1-\delta)^p)^{1/p}\). The average of the disjoint main coordinates has \(p\)-norm at most \(m^{1/p-1}\), and disjointness from the center gives distance at most \((1+m^{1-p})^{1/p}+\eta_\delta\). Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) proves the finite bound; choosing arbitrarily large finite \(m\) inside an infinite index set gives the limit one. No norm attainment is assumed, since every norm-one functional has points arbitrarily close to its supremum.

value.rationale: The result reveals a genuine cardinality effect for a standard thickness invariant: averaging more coordinate slices improves the two-summand scale and in infinite sums forces a universal bound of one, without any Daugavet hypothesis on the factors. This is a natural structural bound rather than an arbitrary estimate.
residual_risks: An older unindexed result may express the same multi-slice containment estimate without Daugavet-index terminology, although the most directly relevant 2014 sums-of-slices paper was read completely.

final_claim: For \(1<p<\infty\), any finite \(n\)-fold \(\ell_p\)-sum of nonzero real Banach spaces satisfies \(\mathcal T^{cc}\le(1+(n-1)^{1-p})^{1/p}\), and every infinite-index \(\ell_p\)-sum satisfies \(\mathcal T^{cc}\le1\).
limitations: Only an upper bound is asserted; optimality for \(n\ge3\) and for infinite index sets is not claimed.
